parts.text:
A curve $C$ is described by the equation
$3x^2+4y^2-2x+6xy-5=0$.
Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at the point $(1,-2)$, giving your answer in the form $ax+by+c=0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Differentiates to obtain: $6x+8y\frac{dy}{dx}-2,\ldots+(6x\frac{dy}{dx}+6y)=0$ M1 A1, +(B1) $\left[\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2-6x-6y}{6x+8y}\right]$
Substitutes $x=1$, $y=-2$ into expression involving $\frac{dy}{dx}$, to give $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{8}{10}$ M1, A1
Uses line equation with numerical 'gradient' $y-(-2)=(\text{their gradient})(x-1)$ or finds $c$ and uses $y=(\text{their gradient})x+"c"$ M1
To give $5y+4x+6=0$ (or equivalent = 0) A1ft [7]

parts.text:

$\int_{1}^{5} \frac{3x}{\sqrt{(2x-1)}} \, dx$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:

and to obtain $u\frac{du}{dx}=\text{const.}$ or equiv. M1

To give 16 cso A1 [8]

(4)

To obtain $A=3$, and $C=4$ A1, A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence, or otherwise, find the series expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$, in ascending powers of $x$, up to and including the term in $x^3$. Simplify each term.
(7)

questions.question_text:
$\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{3x^2+16}{(1-3x)(2+x)^2}=\frac{A}{(1-3x)}+\frac{B}{(2+x)}+\frac{C}{(2+x)^2},\quad |x|<\frac{1}{3}$.
(a) Find the values of $A$ and $C$ and show that $B=0$.
(4)
(b) Hence, or otherwise, find the series expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$, in ascending powers of $x$, up to and including the term in $x^3$. Simplify each term.
(7)
questions.mark_scheme_text:

To obtain $A=3$, and $C=4$ A1, A1

$=3(1+3x,+9x^2+27x^3+\ldots)+$ (M1, A1)

questions.stem: The volume of a spherical balloon of radius $r$ cm is $V$ cm$^3$, where $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
questions.notes: [fix_parts] moved lead-in after (a)'s mark to the start of (b): 'The volume of the balloon increases with time $t$ seconds ac'

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The volume of the balloon increases with time $t$ seconds according to the formula
$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{1000}{(2t+1)^2},\quad t \geqslant 0.$
(b) Using the chain rule, or otherwise, find an expression in terms of $r$ and $t$ for $\frac{dr}{dt}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: Uses $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dt}.\frac{dr}{dV}$ in any form, $=\frac{1000}{4\pi r^2(2t+1)^2}$ M1, A1 (2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Given that $V=0$ when $t=0$, solve the differential equation $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{1000}{(2t+1)^2}$, to obtain $V$ in terms of $t$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$V=\int 1000(2t+1)^{-2}dt$ and integrate to $p(2t+1)^{-1}$, M1, A1
$=-500(2t+1)^{-1}(+c)$ M1
Using $V=0$ when $t=0$ to find $c$, ($c=500$, or equivalent) A1
$\therefore V=500\left(1-\frac{1}{2t+1}\right)$ (any form) (4)

parts.label: d(i)
parts.text:
(d) Hence, at time $t=5$,
(i) find the radius of the balloon, giving your answer to 3 significant figures,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Substitute $t=5$ to give $V$, M1
then use $r=\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3V}{4\pi}\right)}$ to give $r$, $=4.77$ M1, A1 (3)

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) show that the rate of increase of the radius of the balloon is approximately $2.90 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{cm\,s}^{-1}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Substitutes $t=5$ and $r=$ 'their value' into 'their' part (b) M1
$\frac{dr}{dt}=0.0289\ (\approx 2.90\times10^{-2})\ (\text{cm/s})$ * AG A1 (2)
[12]

questions.question_text:
The volume of a spherical balloon of radius $r$ cm is $V$ cm$^3$, where $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
(a) Find $\frac{dV}{dr}$.
(1)
The volume of the balloon increases with time $t$ seconds according to the formula
$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{1000}{(2t+1)^2},\quad t \geqslant 0.$
(b) Using the chain rule, or otherwise, find an expression in terms of $r$ and $t$ for $\frac{dr}{dt}$.
(2)
(c) Given that $V=0$ when $t=0$, solve the differential equation $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{1000}{(2t+1)^2}$, to obtain $V$ in terms of $t$.
(4)
(d) Hence, at time $t=5$,
(i) find the radius of the balloon, giving your answer to 3 significant figures,
(3)
(ii) show that the rate of increase of the radius of the balloon is approximately $2.90 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{cm\,s}^{-1}$.
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$\frac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$ B1 (1)
Uses $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dt}.\frac{dr}{dV}$ in any form, $=\frac{1000}{4\pi r^2(2t+1)^2}$ M1, A1 (2)
$V=\int 1000(2t+1)^{-2}dt$ and integrate to $p(2t+1)^{-1}$, M1, A1
$=-500(2t+1)^{-1}(+c)$ M1
Using $V=0$ when $t=0$ to find $c$, ($c=500$, or equivalent) A1
$\therefore V=500\left(1-\frac{1}{2t+1}\right)$ (any form) (4)
Substitute $t=5$ to give $V$, M1
then use $r=\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3V}{4\pi}\right)}$ to give $r$, $=4.77$ M1, A1 (3)
Substitutes $t=5$ and $r=$ 'their value' into 'their' part (b) M1
$\frac{dr}{dt}=0.0289\ (\approx 2.90\times10^{-2})\ (\text{cm/s})$ * AG A1 (2)
[12]

questions.stem:
The curve shown in Figure 2 has parametric equations
$x=t-2\sin t,\quad y=1-2\cos t,\quad 0 \leqslant t \leqslant 2\pi.$
questions.notes:

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the curve crosses the $x$-axis where $t=\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $t=\frac{5\pi}{3}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Solves $y=0 \Rightarrow \cos t=\frac{1}{2}$ to obtain $t=\frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\frac{5\pi}{3}$ M1
(need both for A1) A1
Or substitutes both values of $t$ and shows that $y=0$ (2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The finite region $R$ is enclosed by the curve and the $x$-axis, as shown shaded in Figure 2.
(b) Show that the area $R$ is given by the integral
$\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{5\pi}{3}} (1-2\cos t)^2 \, dt$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{dx}{dt}=1-2\cos t$ B1
Area$=\int y\,dx=\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{5\pi}{3}}(1-2\cos t)(1-2\cos t)dt$ M1
$=\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{5\pi}{3}}(1-2\cos t)^2 dt$ * AG A1 (3)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use this integral to find the exact value of the shaded area.
TOTAL FOR PAPER: 75 MARKS
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Area $=\int 1-4\cos t+4\cos^2 t\,dt$ 3 terms M1
$=\int 1-4\cos t+2(\cos 2t+1)dt$ (use of correct double angle formula) M1 A1
$=\int 3-4\cos t+2\cos 2t\,dt$
$=[3t-4\sin t+\sin 2t]$ M1 A1
Substitutes the two correct limits $t=\frac{5\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{\pi}{3}$ and subtracts. M1
$=4\pi+3\sqrt{3}$ A1
